record.paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
record.original_question: Is the operator b definable from the rest of the Weihrauch-degree structure, in the setting where ⊔ and ⊓ are known to be definable from ≤W, ∗ is definable from 1, ≤W, and ×, ⋄ is definable from 1, ≤W, and ⋆, and → is definable from ⋆ and ≤W?

evidence.quote: Another line of questions concerns definability of operators from others. As supremum and infimum, we know ⊔ and ⊓ to be definable in terms of ≤W. It is easy to see that ∗ is definable from 1, ≤W and ×, in very much the same way that Westrick’s result has shown ⋄ to be definable from 1, ≤W and ⋆. By definition, → is definable from ⋆ and ≤W. What other definability results can we obtain? In particular, is b definable from the rest of the structure?

artifact.status_search_result: The definability of the operator b within the Weihrauch-degree structure is listed as one of several open definability problems in the area. Recent progress on related questions has been made (e.g., 1 is definable in the Weihrauch degrees, work on the equational theory of the Weihrauch lattice with multiplication, and a study of Weihrauch degrees without roots), but no published resolution of the definability of b from the rest of the structure was found.

status_evidence.title: 1 is definable in the Weihrauch degrees (Lempp, Miller, Pauly, Soskova, Valenti)
status_evidence.snippet: Definability results for operations/constants in the Weihrauch degrees, showing 1 is definable from ≤_W.
status_evidence.claim: Related definability results in the Weihrauch degrees have been established, but the definability of b is not addressed.
